modelAnswer:

question:
(c) Balance the redox reaction below in alkaline medium and identify the oxidizing and reducing agents.
I^- + MnO4^- → IO3^- + MnO2
modelAnswer:
Oxidation half-reaction: I⁻ + 6OH⁻ → IO₃⁻ + 3H₂O + 6e⁻
Reduction half-reaction: MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻

Multiply reduction by 2:
2MnO₄⁻ + 4H₂O + 6e⁻ → 2MnO₂ + 8OH⁻

Add and cancel:
I⁻ + 2MnO₄⁻ + H₂O → IO₃⁻ + 2MnO₂ + 2OH⁻

Oxidizing agent: MnO₄⁻ (Mn reduced from +7 to +4).
Reducing agent: I⁻ (I oxidized from -1 to +5).

(b) (i) The dissociation constant for an acid is a measure of its strength. Use the information in the table below to arrange the following acids in order of increasing acidity.
(ii) Suggest a reason for your arrangement.
modelAnswer:
(i) Order of Increasing Acidity:
CH₃CH₂COOH < CH₂ClCH₂COOH < CH₃CHClCOOH < CH₃CCl₂COOH

(ii) Reason:
Chlorine exerts an electron-withdrawing inductive effect (−I effect) that stabilizes the carboxylate anion, increasing acidity. The closer Cl is to the –COOH group (α > β), the stronger the effect. More Cl atoms = greater cumulative electron withdrawal = stronger acid.

(ii) (a) Vapour pressure lowering: ΔP = X_solute × P°_solvent — solute particles occupy surface, reducing solvent escape.
(b) Freezing point depression: ΔTf = Kf × m — solute disrupts crystal lattice formation.

question:
(d) Arrange the following carboxylic acids in order of increasing acidity. Justify your answer.
3-chloropentanoic acid; pentanoic acid; 2,2-dichloropentanoic acid; 3,3-dichloropentanoic acid; 2-chloropentanoic acid; 4-chloropentanoic acid.
modelAnswer:
Order of increasing acidity:
Pentanoic acid < 4-chloropentanoic acid < 3-chloropentanoic acid < 2-chloropentanoic acid < 3,3-dichloropentanoic acid < 2,2-dichloropentanoic acid

Justification:
Chlorine exerts an electron-withdrawing inductive effect (−I) that stabilizes the carboxylate anion.

The closer Cl is to –COOH (α > β > γ), the stronger the effect.

More Cl atoms = greater electron withdrawal = stronger acid.
